comments.note: usageLine uses nullish coalescing (??) not logical OR (||). An empty string '' would be used as-is rather than falling back to process.argv[1]. This is semantically correct but could surprise a caller who sets usageLine: '' unintentionally. Tests do not cover this case.

parser.ts uses both 'import type' and 'export type' for ParsedArgs — two declarations for the same symbol. This is the idiomatic TypeScript workaround and compiles cleanly, but could be simplified with a single 'export type { ParsedArgs } from' if the local import is not needed. Not a blocking issue.

resolveVersion() has no error boundary around the config.version() function call. If a caller passes a version function that throws, printHelp() will throw uncaught. Acceptable for a library — the caller owns the function — but worth documenting in JSDoc.

comments.note: reviewer-applied-fix: version.ts — extended resolveVersion() JSDoc to note that exceptions from a caller-supplied version() function propagate to the caller. Non-behavioral; documents existing behavior explicitly.

reviewer-applied-fix: help.ts — updated printHelp() JSDoc bullet about the synthetic 'help' entry to reflect the duplicate guard: the entry is suppressed when commands already include id: 'help'. Non-behavioral; corrects an outdated statement in the docstring.

[documentation-forward] resolveVersion() is newly exported in src/version.ts (and re-exported from src/index.ts) but is not documented in README.md. Add a §resolveVersion(config) entry to the README API reference section alongside the other screen/raw-mode exported functions.

parser.ts double-declaration pattern (import type + export type for ParsedArgs) is the only idiomatic TypeScript pattern when a type must be both used locally and re-exported. The parser.test.ts import verifies the re-export works. No simplification is possible while the function's return type annotation requires the local import.

usageLine nullish coalescing (?? vs ||): ?? is the semantically correct choice. The types.ts JSDoc says 'When omitted' — the fallback is defined as triggered by absence (undefined), not falsiness. An explicit usageLine: '' is caller intent and should be honoured.
